Two commercially available 8YSZ ethanol-based suspensions, O-YSZ and T-YSZ, were used for the suspension thermal spray deposition.
The as-sprayed coatings have a high amount of nano-sized porosity with radii below 100 nm, which is greatly reduced after heat treatment at 1100°C.
As the heat treatment temperature increases, the total porosity measured by both neutron scattering and image analysis decreases.
Neutron scattering consistently measures a higher total porosity compared to image analysis, particularly for the as-sprayed and higher temperature heat-treated samples.
The O-YSZ coating shows a sharp increase in porosity measured by neutron scattering at 1200°C, which is not observed in the T-YSZ coating.
The as-sprayed coatings have a metastable tetragonal (t') phase, which starts to decompose into a mixture of tetragonal (t) and cubic (c) phases at 1200°C.
By 1400°C, the phase transformation is complete, with no remaining t' phase and only t and c phases present.

The tetragonality (c/a√2) of the coatings increases from ~1.0096 in the as-sprayed condition to ~1.011 at 1400°C, indicating the transition from the non-transformable t' phase to the transformable t phase.
The O-YSZ coating shows a nearly two-fold increase in crystallite size at 1400°C compared to the T-YSZ coating.
Micro-strain is reduced in both coatings from the as-sprayed condition as the heat treatment temperature increases.
Suspension thermal spray allows the use of sub-micron feedstock particles, enabling finer grain sizes, higher strength, reduced porosity, and enhanced thermal and mechanical properties.
Porosity directly influences the thermal conductivity and strain tolerance of thermal barrier coatings, making its detailed understanding crucial for optimizing coating performance.
The combination of SANS and USANS neutron scattering techniques allows the study of pore sizes ranging from ~1 nm to ~10 μm, covering both the nano-sized and micron-sized porosity features.
Image analysis is limited to pores with sizes above ~100 nm, making it inadequate for the study of suspension thermal sprayed coatings containing pores with radii below 10 nm.
The differences between neutron scattering and image analysis porosity measurements become more apparent at higher heat treatment temperatures as the microstructure evolves.
